handoff.purpose: Module docstring and initial helper definitions: independence rules, label hygiene filters, language families, git wrapper, linked-worktree detection.

symbols.name: _IDENTIFIER_RE
symbols.note: Compiled regex for identifier name-shape check: optional $ or non-digit Unicode letter start, followed by word chars or $.

symbols.name: _JUNK_KEYWORDS
symbols.note: Frozenset of keywords treated as junk labels; case-sensitive, includes control-flow, declaration, literal, and '<anonymous>'.

symbols.name: _LANGUAGE_FAMILIES
symbols.note: Mapping of LanguageSpec names to family names: c/cpp -> c_cpp, javascript/typescript -> js_ts.

symbols.name: _language_family
symbols.note: Returns family key for a language name; None stays None; unknown names map to themselves.

symbols.name: _is_junk_label
symbols.note: Returns True if name fails identifier shape or is in _JUNK_KEYWORDS (case-sensitive).

symbols.name: MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD
symbols.note: Integer 3; number of confirmations required before a mint leaves quarantine.

symbols.name: _GIT_TIMEOUT
symbols.note: Float 30.0; timeout for git subprocess calls.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH
symbols.note: Path to minted_tasks.json in the same directory as this file, derived from __file__.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs git command in repo_root; returns stdout on success, None on any failure (OSError, SubprocessError, non-zero exit).

symbols.name: _is_linked_worktree
symbols.note: Returns True if repo_root is a git linked worktree by inspecting .git file content; incomplete in this chunk.

claims.text: must_include is ONLY: symbols whose extracted source differs between before and after, plus symbols that were added or removed outright. Nothing transitive, ever -- not even 'just one hop of direct callees'.
claims.why: The enforcement is in _mint_from_diffs, not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Minted tasks land with 'tier': 'quarantine' and 'label_provenance': 'independent_diff' and are barred from any go/no-go recall number until confirm_task has been called on them MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD times.
claims.why: Task creation and confirmation logic not in this chunk; MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD is defined but the enforcement is elsewhere.

claims.text: SCOPE: a changed file is eligible as target OR as a label source only if it appears in cached_index(repo)['modules'] -- the exact membership test slice.py's own neighborhood expansion uses (rel in modules, slice.py around line 225; that is THE scope boundary, not a second opinion about it).
claims.why: cached_index is imported, but the scope check is inside _mint_from_diffs not present here.

claims.text: Changed files that fail this test are recorded in skipped_out_of_scope on the diagnostics returned alongside the task (and on the task itself when one is minted) -- never silently dropped.
claims.why: Recording logic is in _mint_from_diffs, not present here.

claims.text: CROSS-FILE ONLY: must_include never contains a symbol defined in the file chosen as target. ... A commit/edit where only one in-scope file has any diffed symbols therefore has no valid label source at all: it mints nothing rather than minting a label=[] task ... THE SAME GUARD APPLIES AFTER LABEL HYGIENE BELOW: ... _mint_from_diffs re-checks non-emptiness once, after filtering, and mints nothing (with a reason) if nothing survives.
claims.why: Enforcement is in _mint_from_diffs, not present here.

claims.text: JUNK: a diffed name that fails _is_junk_label (not a plausible identifier under any supported language's rules, or one of a small set of node-text markers that are never legitimate exported symbol names in ANY of them -- if/<anonymous>/etc.) never becomes a must_include entry -- dropped names land in labels_filtered_junk (sorted).
claims.why: _is_junk_label is defined here and its behavior matches the described junk filter (identifier shape + keyword set). The recording into labels_filtered_junk is in _mint_from_diffs, so that part is uncheckable. Overall verdict: kept for the filter behavior, uncheckable for the recording.

claims.text: CROSS-LANGUAGE: a label may only come from a file whose language FAMILY (_language_family(languages.spec_for(...).name)) matches the TARGET's ... Filtered names land in labels_filtered_cross_language (sorted).
claims.why: _language_family is defined here, but the cross-language filter application is in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule is run against every anchor CANDIDATE's current content before target selection. A file that trips the floor is dropped from the ANCHOR POOL (recorded in skipped_secret_floor) ... AND from label consideration ... Filtered names land in labels_filtered_secret_floor (sorted).
claims.why: secret_floor_rule is imported, but the exclusion logic is in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: Name-shape check: unicode-aware (a non-ASCII identifier -- café -- is legal Python/JS/etc and must not be treated as noise just for using non-ASCII letters) and allows a leading/embedded $ (legal anywhere in a JS/TS identifier, e.g. Angular's $scope) on top of the universal letter/digit/underscore identifier shape.
claims.why: _IDENTIFIER_RE = ^(?:[^\W\d]|\$)[\w$]*$ matches Unicode letters (via [^\W\d] which includes Unicode word chars minus digits), allows leading $, and allows embedded $ via [\w$]*.

claims.text: Keyword check: deliberately NARROW, and case-SENSITIVE. ... The set below is further limited to words that are reserved in EVERY supported language and implausible as a real symbol name in any of them -- unlike new/delete/default/case/switch/static/of/in, which are ordinary, common identifiers in at least one supported language ...
claims.why: The set contains words like 'if', 'else', 'class', 'def', 'true', 'false', 'null', etc., which are reserved in many languages; it excludes 'new', 'delete', 'default', 'case', 'switch', 'static', 'of', 'in' as claimed. The check in _is_junk_label is case-sensitive (name in _JUNK_KEYWORDS, no lowercasing).

claims.text: The keyword check is intentionally case-SENSITIVE ... name is matched as-is, never lowercased.
claims.why: _is_junk_label returns name in _JUNK_KEYWORDS directly, no lowercasing.

claims.text: True if name cannot be a real symbol label -- see the JUNK FILTER comment above. Checked name-shape-first (a non-identifier like <anonymous> never reaches the keyword set at all).
claims.why: _is_junk_label first checks _IDENTIFIER_RE.match(name); if it fails, returns True immediately, so keyword set is not consulted.

claims.text: Below this many independent confirmations a mint stays quarantined and is excluded from go/no-go. Rationale: ... Three independent mints landing on the same must_include set is a defensible floor ...
claims.why: MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD is defined as 3, matching the rationale. The enforcement is elsewhere, but the constant value is correct.

claims.text: Persisted mint store -- the load path that was missing entirely before this fix. ... Sibling of harness.py's DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH: same directory, same 'JSON file, sorted keys, schema-versioned' contract. Absence of the file (a fresh checkout, or a repo where nothing has ever been minted) means 'nothing minted yet', not an error -- see load_minted_tasks.
claims.why: DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH is defined here, but load_minted_tasks is not in this chunk; the contract claims are about that function.

claims.text: Run git in repo_root; stdout on success, None on ANY failure (missing git, not a repo, bad ref, timeout, non-zero exit). Minting must degrade to 'nothing minted', never raise -- a caller looping over commits or landed edits cannot be allowed to die on the first unreadable one.
claims.why: _git catches (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) and returns None; also returns None on non-zero returncode. It does not raise on those failures. Timeout is covered by subprocess.TimeoutExpired which is a SubprocessError.

claims.text: True if repo_root is a git LINKED WORKTREE, not a primary checkout.
claims.why: The function is incomplete in this chunk; the final return logic is not shown, so the overall truth value cannot be verified.

claims.text: A minted task stores repo as an ABSOLUTE PATH (see _mint_from_diffs) and the mint store is append-only, so that path has to stay resolvable for the whole life of the corpus. A linked worktree is by construction temporary: daedalus.spine.attempt creates one per candidate and deletes it in a finally:. Minting from one therefore writes a task that can NEVER be evaluated again ...
claims.why: References _mint_from_diffs and daedalus.spine.attempt which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Detection is the git on-disk contract, not a path heuristic: git worktree add writes .git as a FILE holding a gitdir: pointer, whereas a primary checkout has .git as a DIRECTORY. A bare repo and a plain non-repo directory both read as 'not a linked worktree' and are left to the existing git-failure paths, which already degrade to 'nothing minted'.
claims.why: The visible code checks dot_git.is_file() and returns False if it is not a file, which matches the claim.

claims.text: The pointer alone is NOT enough, and this was measured rather than assumed: a SUBMODULE also has .git as a gitdir: file, and a submodule checkout is perfectly permanent -- refusing to mint from one would be a false refusal, and a docstring saying 'linked worktree' while the code also caught submodules would be a claim its control did not implement.
claims.why: The code checks the pointer but does not yet distinguish submodule vs worktree; the structural inspection is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Nor is the pointer's PATH enough: matching a worktrees path component would fire on any ordinary repository that happens to live under a directory someone named worktrees. So the admin directory the pointer resolves to is inspected STRUCTURALLY, which is what actually distinguishes them ... commondir and gitdir together appear only in the linked-worktree admin layout. Requiring BOTH means an unreadable or unexpected target fails toward 'not ephemeral', i.e. toward minting -- which is the correct direction for a false negative here, because the alternative is refusing to mint from ordinary repositories.
claims.why: The structural inspection (checking for commondir and gitdir files) is not in this chunk; it likely appears in the next lines.

observations.what: Module docstring makes many promises about _mint_from_diffs behavior (scope, cross-file, label hygiene, secret floor) but that function is not in this chunk.
_is_linked_worktree is cut off mid-implementation; the structural inspection described in its docstring is not visible.

The junk keyword set includes words like 'pass', 'def', 'class' that are common identifiers in some languages (e.g., 'pass' is not a keyword in Go, 'class' is a common identifier in Python contexts though it is a keyword in Python itself). The comment claims the set is limited to words reserved in EVERY supported language, but 'pass' is not reserved in Go, 'def' is not in Go, 'class' is not in Go, 'true'/'false' are not in Python, etc. This may over-filter real symbols.
_language_family groups only c/cpp and javascript/typescript; the comment claims these are the only pairs the import graph routinely crosses, but this is not verifiable from this chunk.
